project: quay-krewe: a project carries its own context

user_actions.1: A project holds a brief and a design, and any write to the design clears the approval.
user_actions.2: The design carries a numbered path of atomised changes.
user_actions.3: Julian takes a step, and the session starts holding what it needs.
user_actions.4: Julian reads the state of the path.
user_actions.5: A step records what came of it.

rules: One intention per slice. One reviewable pull request per slice. Revertable alone.
Every slice ships its scenarios in the same change. The promises gate refuses a behaviour change that carries no scenario.
Each slice is written for somebody who was not in the design conversation.
S-5 is the gate. If the measurement says no, every slice after it is cancelled.
Tests never run on this machine. Continuous integration is the test runner. The safe local gates are go build, go vet, gofmt and golangci-lint.

slices.name: The dead role brief path is removed
slices.intention: Clear a trap before anybody builds on it.
slices.changes: renderContext no longer holds an unassigned brief, an always false branch, or a RoleScope section. sandbox.Config loses its Role field, so layout and conversationDir each have one path instead of two. The read back in syncContextExcept stops naming RoleScope.
slices.proves: features/context.feature gains a scenario saying a memory file carries no role section. Every existing context and directories scenario stays green.
slices.why_first: internal/controlplane/server.go lines 585 to 599 look exactly like a working mechanism for handing a session a brief. It is inert. Anybody who builds S-3 will find it and believe it.

slices.name: The linter refuses an always false branch
slices.intention: Make the class of defect S-1 removed impossible to add back.
slices.changes: staticcheck joins the enabled linter set, so an always false condition and an assigned but unused value fail the lint job.
slices.risk: staticcheck may report findings elsewhere in the module. This slice fixes every finding it raises, or the linter entry does not go in. A finding whose fix touches a .go file needs a scenario, or the pull request body carries a No scenario line with a reason.
slices.why_after_s1: Added before S-1, it turns the build red on code that is about to go anyway.

slices.name: A project carries a design
slices.intention: Give a project somewhere to keep what it is for and what was designed.

partial_contracts.TABLE-1: The columns migration 0062 adds. The approval columns come in S-6.

slices.changes: A new table, three store methods against both implementations, a Design message, three remote procedure calls, and the words krewe design, krewe design brief and krewe design set. Nothing renders into a sandbox yet.
slices.proves: features/design.feature. Set a brief and read it back. Set a design body and read it back whole. Writing a body over an approved design is proved in S-6, because approval does not exist yet.
slices.note: internal/controlplane/design.go is new, beside capability.go and hooks_render.go, following how server.go is already split.

slices.name: The design reaches the session working in the project
slices.intention: Put the design in front of the model, cheaply.

partial_contracts.RENDER-1: Line 1 and the first sentence of line 3. Line 2 comes in S-6, the rest of line 3 in S-9, and line 4 in S-10.

slices.changes: renderContext gains one section at the top of the inner memory file, under a new design mark. The section names the project, the brief and the design file. The whole design body is written to .krewe/design.md in the session's working directory on every render.
slices.proves: features/design.feature. A session dispatched into a project with a design reads the summary in its memory file and the body in .krewe/design.md. A scenario measures the section at under 400 characters with a 5000 character brief.
slices.note: The design mark must be named in the read back scope list in syncContextExcept. Text under a mark the build does not know is swept into the session's own context, which is the trap RoleScope documented.

slices.name: The riskiest assumption is measured
slices.intention: Answer the one question that decides whether the rest is worth building.
slices.changes: Nothing in the product. One dated entry in the decisions file.
slices.proves: The entry names both dispatches, what came back, and whether Julian accepts the work. It is an observation, never an inference.
slices.gate: Every slice after this one waits for Julian to read the entry and say the next move. If the answer is no, they are cancelled. The cost so far is one migration and one render.

slices.name: A design carries an approval only the operator can grant
slices.intention: Make Julian's word a fact the system holds, and tie it to a specific text.

partial_contracts.TABLE-1: The approved and approved_at columns, in migration 0063.

slices.changes: Two columns, one store method, one remote procedure call, the word krewe design approve, and one entry in DeniedToDriver. SetProjectDesign now clears the approval in the same write as the body.
slices.proves: features/design.feature. Approve, rewrite, then read: the approval is gone. Approving an empty design is refused. A driver session that tries to approve is refused, and the refusal says it is the operator's to make.
slices.note: Clearing the approval on a body write is the same column and the same write. Shipping the two apart would leave a state where an approved row carries a body nobody approved.

slices.name: The operator edits a design body in the editor
slices.intention: Make writing a design as easy as writing context.
slices.changes: krewe design edit fetches the body, opens VISUAL then EDITOR then vi, and sends what was saved back through SetDesign.
slices.proves: features/design.feature, with the editor doubled the way krewe context edit is already tested. Editing and saving writes the new text into the store.
slices.note: This slice needs no approval and no path, so it can be built beside S-6 and S-8.

slices.name: A project holds a numbered path of steps
slices.intention: Give a project somewhere to keep the atomised changes.

partial_contracts.STORE-5: The replace. Protecting a step somebody took comes in S-12, because no step can be taken yet.
partial_contracts.WIRE-7: Every refusal except the one that protects a taken step.
partial_contracts.WIRE-8: The listing. The next field comes in S-13.
partial_contracts.COMMAND-6: The listing. The next line comes in S-13.

slices.changes: A second table, two store methods, a Step message, two remote procedure calls, the path document grammar in the control plane, and the words krewe path and krewe path set.
slices.proves: features/path.feature. Set a path of five steps and read it back in number order. A document with a duplicate number is refused, naming both lines. A document with no step heading is refused.
slices.note: The control plane parses the document, so the console and the command line send the same words. This is the same reason the control plane composes the step text.

slices.name: The path document reaches the session working in the project
slices.intention: Let a session read what the steps before it produced.

partial_contracts.RENDER-1: The second sentence of line 3, naming .krewe/path.md.
partial_contracts.RENDER-3: The whole file. The result line is empty until S-11 exists.

slices.changes: Every render writes .krewe/path.md into the session's working directory, one block per step in number order.
slices.proves: features/path.feature. A session dispatched into a project with a path reads every step in .krewe/path.md, in number order.
slices.why_before_s10: The step text S-10 composes names .krewe/path.md. A pointer to a file that is not there sends the model to open nothing.

slices.name: The operator takes a step
slices.intention: Start a session that already knows the design, the project and the one change it is taking.

partial_contracts.RENDER-1: Line 4, the step this session took.

slices.changes: Two store methods, one remote procedure call, the text composition, and the word krewe step take. The step text is the dispatch text, so Dispatch is untouched.
slices.proves: features/path.feature. Taking a step dispatches a session whose text names the step. Taking it twice is refused, naming the session that holds it. Taking a step on an unapproved design is refused and starts nothing.
slices.note: This is the only gate in the work, and it refuses one of Julian's own commands. A refusal costs one line of output and starts nothing. Nothing dispatches a session without Julian asking.

slices.name: A step records what came of it
slices.intention: Keep what somebody said a step produced, so the next session starts from what is true.

partial_contracts.RENDER-3: The result line of a finished step.
partial_contracts.COMMAND-9: The done line. The next step line comes in S-13.

slices.changes: One store method, one remote procedure call, and the words krewe step done and krewe step stop. A finished step carries its result into .krewe/path.md.
slices.proves: features/path.feature. A finished step carries its result into the path document, so the next session reads what the last one produced. Finishing with a word that is not done or stopped is refused. Finishing with no result is refused.
slices.note: A step's finish is what somebody declared, never what the system observed. Nothing can see inside a container.

slices.name: Replacing a path protects the steps somebody already took
slices.intention: Stop a rewritten path from losing the record of work that happened.

partial_contracts.STORE-5: The protection. The replace shipped in S-8.
partial_contracts.WIRE-7: The FailedPrecondition that names the protected steps.

slices.changes: SetPath refuses a document that drops or renames a step in state taken, done or stopped. The refusal names those numbers. A refused write changes nothing.
slices.proves: features/path.feature. Take step 2, then set a path without it: refused, naming step 2. Set a path without step 2 while it is ready: it goes.
slices.why_after_s10: Before a step can be taken, the rule is unreachable and no scenario can prove it.

slices.name: The path says which step is next
slices.intention: Put the operator's next command in front of them.

partial_contracts.COMMAND-6: The next line under the listing.
partial_contracts.COMMAND-9: The next line in the output of krewe step done.

slices.changes: ListStepsResponse carries next, the lowest numbered ready step whose predecessor is done. krewe path prints it under the listing, and krewe step done prints it after finishing one.
slices.proves: features/path.feature. A path with steps 1 and 2 done says step 3 is next. A path where every ready step waits on something unfinished says nothing is next.
slices.note: Nothing advances by itself. The next step is a sentence, never a dispatch.

slices.name: The operator reads one step whole
slices.intention: Show the intention, the touches and the proof, which no row of a listing can hold.
slices.changes: krewe step show prints one step whole, including its state, the session that took it and its result.
slices.proves: features/path.feature. Showing a step prints its intention, touches and proof whole. Showing a number the path does not have is refused, saying how many steps there are.

slices.name: A skill teaches a session to design a project
slices.intention: Let an ordinary session carry the ideation and the design, with no machinery around it.
slices.changes: One skill, prose only, no code. It tells a session to read the brief and the repository, write the design, write the path in the grammar, and never approve.
slices.proves: features/design.feature. A session dispatched with the skill writes a design and a path that read back whole, and the design it wrote is not approved.
slices.note: This is the headline capability and it comes near the end on purpose. It rests on the design reaching a session. If that does not help, the ideation conversation is not worth building.

slices.name: The console draws a project's path
slices.intention: Let the operator read the path without leaving the console.
slices.changes: A path resource, drilled into from a project. Columns: number, title, state, session, age. Enter descends into the project's sessions when the step names one.
slices.proves: internal/console table tests for the columns, the order and the refusal. features/console.feature for the view opening by name.
slices.note: SortBy is -1. The control plane answers in number order, and sorting rendered text would put step 10 above step 2.

slices.name: The project row counts the steps that are done
slices.intention: Say how far a project has got, on the listing an operator already reads.
slices.changes: The projects view gains a path column reading done out of total. One ListSteps call per draw, not one per project.
slices.proves: internal/console table tests. A project with seven steps, three done, draws 3/7. A project with no path draws an empty cell.
slices.note: Project gains no field on the wire. The count is derived by the reader.
